title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Maya Kapoor
description: Motivation: The continuous batching scheduler has intermittently favored large low-priority requests under mixed workloads, causing head-of-line blocking and p99 latency spikes on latency-sensitive routes. This PR tunes queueing and timeout logic to improve fairness and prevent starvation while keeping throughput stable. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces hop-based aging: requests accrue an aging score as they wait, which gradually increases their scheduling priority relative to new requests. 2) Adds per-queue soft timeouts and escalations: if a request waits beyond a soft timeout we move it to an escalated queue with higher scheduling weight; hard timeouts remain unchanged to bound latency. 3) Tightens batch formation window for high-priority routes to reduce enqueueing latency while preserving batching efficiency for throughput routes. 4) Adds metrics and dashboards for aging, escalations, and timeout hits. 5) New unit and integration tests that simulate mixed priority workloads and verify no starvation for high-priority small requests. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2421) - [x] Benchmarked on perf-lab against representative traces - [x] Added unit + integration tests - [x] Added metrics and dashboard panels - [x] CI green except transient flaky test rerun Related: Linear ENG-2421, ENG-2568. See perf numbers in description below. Implementation notes: - Aging is implemented as a monotonically increasing uint32 per-request counter incremented on each scheduler cycle; it is folded into the scheduler weight as weight = base_weight + alpha * aging_score. Alpha is configurable via config/scheduler.toml. - Escalation uses two soft timeout thresholds: soft_ttl_ms (default 50ms) and escalate_ttl_ms (default 200ms). Soft hits move requests into an escalated FIFO sub-queue; escalated requests are favored but still batched where possible. - High-priority routes are annotated via route metadata; batch_window_ms is reduced for these routes to allow quicker dispatch when low-occupancy. - Metric names added: continuous_batcher.request_aging, continuous_batcher.escalations, continuous_batcher.soft_timeout_hits, continuous_batcher.hard_timeout_drops. Perf summary (perf-lab, mixed workload trace A): - Baseline median latency: 12.3ms -> unchanged - Baseline p95: 38.2ms -> 33.1ms (-13.3%) - Baseline p99: 54.0ms -> 44.4ms (-17.8%) - Throughput (tokens/s) change: -1.2% (within noise) - 99.9th percentile of escalation rate: 0.8% (low) Tests: - Unit tests cover aging math, escalation transition, and priority invariants. - Integration test simulates 10k requests with 20% high-priority small requests interleaved with large low-priority requests; verified no starvation and lower p99. Rollout plan: feature gated behind continuous_batcher.experimental.scheduler_tuning; enable on canary fleet for 48h, then ramp. Files changed (high level): - scheduler/continuous_batcher/scheduler.rs (core tuning) - scheduler/continuous_batcher/config.rs (new config knobs) - scheduler/continuous_batcher/tests/mixed_workload.rs (integration) - metrics/metrics_registry.rs (new metrics) - telemetry/dashboards/continuous_batcher.jsonnet (dashboard panels) - docs/rfcs/2026-02-continuous-batcher-scheduling.md (design summary) - Cargo.toml CI: runs unit, integration, lint, and perf smoke tests. Non-goals: this PR does not change kernel execution, KV cache behavior, or inference runtime internals; those will be addressed in follow-ups.

release_notes: Tune continuous batcher scheduler to reduce p99 latency under mixed workloads by adding request aging, escalation queues, and configurable soft timeouts. Rollout behind feature flag.
